title: Single Monolithic Database Access (Monolith Database Integration)
pattern: All application sub-modules and classes share a single database connection instance with unrestricted, unsegmented SQL read and write permissions to the entire database schema.
why_bad: Encapsulation is completely broken. Payment modules can accidentally modify unrelated user records. A bug in one module can corrupt the database of another, leading to a catastrophic blast radius.
detection: All modules within a large codebase importing and executing raw SQL transactions against arbitrary tables from a single database client reference.
counterexample: Small CRUD systems where database access controls do not add architectural value.
fix:
Logically partition the database into schemas and restrict the database credentials utilized by different modules or services to their specific domains.
```rust
// PaymentModule holds restricted connection to payment schema only
```
source: Heather Adkins et al., *Building Secure and Reliable Systems* (2020), Chapter 6 ("Example Architecture of a monolithic web app"); Martin Kleppmann, *Designing Data-Intensive Applications* (2017), Chapter 11 ("Replication and Consistency").
